title: Private Day-2: Backup/Restore + DR toolkit requirements and acceptance criteria
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Ship a supported, documented, repeatable Day-2 operations toolkit for Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem/air-gapped) to enable customers and Redwood teams to:
1) take consistent backups of control-plane and critical configuration state
2) restore reliably into a new or existing cluster
3) execute DR procedures that meet enterprise RPO/RTO targets

Why now
- Enterprise pipeline blockers: FinBank (VPC) and MedData Systems (on-prem/air-gapped) have made DR readiness a procurement gate.
- Support signals: repeated asks for an “official” runbook + clear support boundaries.
- Product maturity: Private is expanding; Day-2 readiness must be part of the baseline offer.

- Product: Vivek Kulkarni (owner), Talia Benson (PgM)
- Eng: Ethan Park (control plane), Priya Natarajan (sponsor)
- SRE/Reliability: Sean Gallagher (runbooks/on-call), Neha Kapoor (reliability sponsor), Rafael Mendes (game day)
- Security: Marcus Lin (lead), Hanae Suzuki (secrets/KMS)
- Release Eng: Connor O’Brien, Sahana Iyer
- Solutions: Markus Klein (customer workflows), Fatima Noor (on-prem validation), Colin O’Donnell (VPC validation)

- Spec draft: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/private-deployments/day2-backup-restore-spec-draft.json
- Customer survey: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/private-deployments/customer-requirements-backup-restore-survey.json
- DR game day notes: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/dr-gameday-notes-2025-02-14.json
- ADR (backup format + encryption): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-027-backup-format-and-encryption.json

In-scope (must support)
A) Control-plane backup/restore (Redwood Private)
- Control-plane stateful datastores (configuration DB, policy/routing config store, etc.)
- Kubernetes manifests/Helm release values required to deterministically recreate control plane
- References to secrets (NOT raw secret material) and integration configuration (KMS key IDs, secret manager paths, cert manager config) sufficient to rehydrate on restore
- Restore validation hooks (health checks + functional smoke tests)

B) DR procedures + Day-2 operationalization
- Runbooks for: routine backups, on-demand backups, restore to new cluster, restore into existing cluster (where safe/defined), DR in defined archetypes
- Observability: success/failure metrics, dashboards, and alerting for backup jobs and restore drills
- “Game day validated” end-to-end rehearsal in Redwood staging; publish write-up and resulting action items

C) Packaging for constrained environments
- On-prem/air-gapped: signed offline bundle layout, deterministic artifacts, checksum manifest, offline docs
- VPC: guidance for S3/KMS/IAM (least privilege) and restore staging patterns

Out of scope (explicit)
- Backing up customer prompts, model weights, or customer application data beyond Redwood control-plane state.
- “Full cluster snapshot restore” as the primary/only path (e.g., etcd restore) — can be referenced as break-glass infra procedure but not required for standard Redwood Private restore.
- Cross-cloud provider migrations as a first-class supported workflow in v1 (document as best-effort / consultative only).
- Automatic failover between active-active regions (v1 focuses on documented DR + staged restore).

Supported environments (v1)
1) VPC deployments
- Single-region, multi-AZ Kubernetes cluster
- Single-region, single-AZ (allowed for non-prod; docs must call out risk)
- Storage backend: S3-compatible object store for backup artifacts (AWS S3 as reference; S3-compatible OK if it meets API + durability requirements)

2) On-prem deployments
- Connected on-prem (limited egress allowed) with NFS or S3-compatible object store
- Air-gapped (no external calls): NFS-backed backups and/or local object storage; offline artifact import/export required

Backup artifact requirements
- Backup must be consistent (documented pre-flight checks + quiesce behavior where necessary).
- Artifact must be encrypted at rest.
  - Default: envelope encryption with a data key; encrypted data key stored alongside artifact.
  - KMS: support customer-managed keys where applicable (cloud KMS or HSM-backed provider; exact providers in ENG-9823).
- Integrity verification: checksums (sha256) + manifest describing contents, versions, and restore prerequisites.
- Deterministic layout: consistent file naming, versioned format, and clear compatibility rules.
- Retention: provide recommended defaults (e.g., 14/30/90 days) and guidance for audit/compliance; actual retention is customer-configured.

RPO/RTO targets (product requirements)
- Provide a published target matrix by archetype and component (see Confluence matrix deliverable). Targets should be framed as “achievable with recommended architecture and backup cadence,” not an unconditional SLA.
- Baseline targets for reference architectures:
  - VPC single-region / multi-AZ: RPO <= 1 hour (with hourly backups), RTO <= 4 hours (staged restore to clean cluster)
  - On-prem connected: RPO <= 4 hours, RTO <= 8 hours (depends on storage + cluster provisioning)
  - Air-gapped: RPO <= 24 hours (typical operational cadence), RTO <= 24 hours (manual steps + offline artifact handling)

Acceptance criteria (Definition of Done)
1) Backup
- Operator can run: `private-installer backup create` (or equivalent documented entrypoint) and produce a backup artifact + manifest.
- Backup includes:
  - Control-plane state (datastores) required to recreate tenant configuration and routing policies
  - Helm release values / manifests required to re-deploy control plane deterministically
  - References to secrets/KMS (no raw secret contents)
- Backup encryption:
  - Encrypted artifact by default
  - KMS integration path documented + validated in at least one reference cloud environment
- Verification:
  - Backup command prints verification results (checksum + manifest validation)
  - Artifact can be listed/inspected safely without decryption of payload (manifest readable)

2) Restore
- Operator can run: `private-installer restore apply --from <artifact>` to a clean target cluster.
- Restore performs:
  - Pre-flight checks (cluster access, required CRDs present, storage backend reachable, version compatibility)
  - Bootstrap ordering documented and automated as much as feasible
  - Post-restore validation report (human-readable + machine-readable JSON output) covering component health and minimum functional checks
- Clear abort/rollback criteria documented (when to stop, what state is safe/unsafe, how to retry).

3) Documentation (internal + customer-facing)
- Internal Confluence runbooks published and reviewed by SRE + Security:
  - Control-plane backup runbook
  - Control-plane restore runbook
  - Data-plane/state guidance page (stateless restore patterns)
  - DR plan: VPC single-region
  - DR plan: on-prem air-gapped
  - Storage backends guide (S3+KMS, NFS, optional GCS where applicable)
  - Velero / K8s backup tooling integration guidance (include/exclude lists)
- Customer-facing docs (docs site) published with:
  - What is backed up / not backed up
  - How to schedule backups
  - How to perform a restore to a clean cluster
  - DR checklist and “how to test your restore” section
  - Troubleshooting guide (common errors: RBAC, CRDs missing, KMS unavailable, storage slow)
  - Support boundaries (what Support can advise vs requires PS/Solutions)

4) Observability + on-call readiness
- Metrics emitted:
  - backup_success_total / backup_failure_total
  - backup_duration_seconds
  - backup_bytes_written
  - backup_last_success_timestamp
  - restore_drill_success_total / restore_drill_failure_total
  - restore_drill_duration_seconds
- Dashboard in observability pack showing:
  - last_success_ts and duration (with thresholds)
  - failure rate over 7/30 days
  - restore drill cadence and outcomes
- Alerts:
  - Page for production when backup has not succeeded within configured SLO window (with maintenance window suppression guidance)
  - Non-prod alerts can be ticket/Slack only (no paging) by default

5) Validation / game day
- Automated restore drill in Redwood staging runs on a scheduled cadence (at least weekly).
- One formal DR game day executed and documented (timeline, MTTR, issues, remediation tickets).

Non-functional requirements
- Least privilege: IAM/RBAC examples must be minimal and scoped; docs must provide recommended policies.
- Works in restricted environments: no hard dependency on outbound internet for on-prem restore path.
- Deterministic bundle layout for air-gapped installs with signature verification.
- Version compatibility defined:
  - Backup format versioning
  - Supported restore paths (same minor version; N-1 -> N defined if supported)
  - Clear error messages if incompatibility detected.

Open questions / decisions needed (tracked here until resolved)
- Which exact datastores comprise “control-plane state” for v1, and how do we guarantee consistency (quiesce vs transactional snapshot)? (Owner: Ethan Park)
- Final list of supported KMS providers for envelope encryption (AWS KMS is minimum; others best-effort?) (Owner: Hanae Suzuki / Marcus Lin)
- Are we shipping Velero as a recommended dependency or “optional integration guide only”? (Owner: Sean Gallagher / Vivek Kulkarni)
- Restore into existing cluster: do we support in-place restore for same cluster (corruption scenarios) or only “restore to clean cluster”? (Owner: Miles Thornton)

Customer inputs summarized (from survey + calls)
- FinBank (VPC): asks for RPO <= 1h, RTO <= 4h; requires customer-managed KMS key; wants documented restore validation and evidence.
- MedData Systems (on-prem air-gapped): requires offline bundles with signatures, no external calls; prefers NFS; needs audit log export/retention guidance.

Release / rollout notes
- This ticket is the PM requirements umbrella for ENG work. Feature flags and “beta” labeling are acceptable for initial release, but docs must be explicit about limitations.
- GA readiness requires: security review sign-off on encryption and secret-handling; SRE sign-off on alerts and runbooks; Release Eng sign-off on signing/offline bundle verification.

Updates
- 2025-02-18 (Vivek): Requirements aligned with SRE + Security; added explicit acceptance criteria for ‘no raw secrets’ and for machine-readable restore report. Game day outcome items incorporated from 2025-02-14 notes; prioritizing CRD ordering + RBAC hardening as known restore failure modes.
